Sofia / team — taking the dataflow and subprocessor sections. Summary below (I filled the SSQ tab 'Dataflow & Subprocessors'):

- Dataflow (high-level):
  * Ingest: customer requests (API or private deployment) -> front-end ingress (load balancer) -> request sanitized/prefix stripped by proxy.
  * Tokenization: For hosted customers using our Redwood API, we perform transient tokenization at the edge (ephemeral tokens stored in encrypted KV for the request lifetime). Raw identifiers are not persisted in production telemetry.
  * Processing: Inference runtime (GPU pool) holds ephemeral KV cache for sequence context — caches are zeroed on eviction and never written to long-term storage.
  * Persistence: Customer-specified artifacts (logs, embeddings) are optional; default hosted retention is 30 days for telemetry and 90 days for metrics; customers can opt into shorter retention or Private deployment.
  * Pseudonymization: We replace direct identifiers with one-way hashes before any long-term storage; any reversible mapping is kept only in customer-managed key environments (Private deploy / Bring-Your-Own-Key).

- Subprocessors (current roster, role, region):
  * FastCache Inc. — distributed KV cache provider (edge caching) — us, eu
  * CloudOps Storage (object store) — storage of optional artifacts (encrypted-at-rest) — us
  * AnalyticsPartner LLP — anonymized telemetry aggregation — us
  * ThirdPartyOps (managed infra) — limited 管理 access for incident response (US only)

None of the above have access to unredacted PII except under documented, time-limited incident response procedures; the SSQ sheet marks which subprocessors see identifiers.

Looping in privileged access controls and evidence. Key points to surface for MedSafe: 

- Role-based access: engineers have scoped roles. There are distinct roles: inference-ops (no raw data exports), infra-ops (limited runtime debugging with redact-first tooling), and privacy-audit (read-only access to anonymized artifacts).
- Break-glass: emergency access requires two-person approval + automated time-limited credential issuance; all sessions are recorded.
- Auditing: all access to systems that can potentially touch identifiers is logged (W3C-style request traces), immutable logs are pushed to our write-once log store for 365 days. Audit trails include who, when, justification.
- Sample evidence: kms-attestation-2028-03.pdf (HSM attestation for our hosted KMS), and a redacted access log sample (we will scrub customer identifiers before sharing).

I recommend we include the following in the consolidated reply to MedSafe: the filled SSQ, the diagram, the KMS attestation PDF, and a redacted log sample. I can prepare the log sample by EOD Wed.

Ben Carter
